Another day, another D.C. band-aid on a bullet wound. The Preparing for the Future Act throws $8,000 grants at psychology students while the 2024 Fitzpatrick-Chu bill offered $200k loan forgiveness for professionals committing five years. This half-measure creates more bureaucracy without solving the core problem - schools need immediate staffing, not delayed promises.

Section 2(b)(3) even converts grants to loans if service obligations aren’t met, setting up students for debt traps. Meanwhile, the Department of Education’s own data shows 70% of similar grant programs fail to meet retention targets.

Real solutions require dismantling credentialing cartels that block workforce entry, not subsidizing academia’s failure to produce enough graduates.

The Trump administration's freeze on HIV prevention funding was a necessary correction to decades of fiscal negligence, redirecting billions from unchecked foreign aid and bureaucratic bloat to prioritize American taxpayers. While activists frame this as "cuts," it's accountability—forcing agencies to justify every dollar instead of rubber-stamping failed programs.

The Public Health Funding Restoration Act (S.786) proves the problem: throwing $2B at prevention slush funds without auditing existing waste. CDC's reversal isn't "restoring science"—it's surrendering to the same lobbyists who let HIV spending balloon while outcomes stagnate.

Real public health starts with auditing grift, not funding every identity-based program that claims moral urgency.

The real issue isn't funding delays—it's systemic bureaucratic bloat. Head Start's $12B budget gets funneled through layers of administrative waste while classrooms suffer. The program's regional offices and grant processes exemplify government inefficiency, with 37% less funding distributed this year due to D.C.'s inability to streamline operations.

Rather than throwing more taxpayer money into a broken system, we need structural reforms that bypass federal middlemen. True early education support comes from redirecting funds to state-managed programs with direct accountability, not sustaining a 60-year-old federal monolith that's become a jobs program for bureaucrats.

Audit the waste, empower local control, and watch classrooms flourish without D.C.'s incompetence.
